ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a small ball, which can be considered as a particle, is thrown vertically upward from a height $H$ above the ground with an initial velocity $v_{0}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. On the ground, there is a small cart of length $L{=}5\mathrm{m}$, with its front end $M$ located $s{=}4\mathrm{m}$ horizontally from the point directly below the launch point. At the same time the ball is thrown, the cart starts moving to the right with a constant acceleration from rest. It is known that the speed of the ball when it hits the ground is $20\mathrm{m/s}$. Neglect air resistance and the height of the cart, and take the gravitational acceleration $g$ as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Determine the time $t$ it takes for the ball to travel from the point of projection to the ground and the height $H$ of the projection point above the ground.
2. To ensure that the cart catches the ball, determine the range of the cart's acceleration $a$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The figure shows a ball above the ground on a vertical dashed line, with an upward initial velocity arrow labeled v0. The height from the ground to the projection point is labeled H. A cart lies on the ground to the left of the vertical dashed line; its right/front end is labeled M and its left/rear end is labeled N. The horizontal distance from M to the point directly below the ball is labeled s = 4 m. Reasoning following the assigned method: Take upward as positive. The ball is thrown upward with v0 = 10 m/s, acceleration is -g = -10 m/s^2, and at ground impact the velocity is downward, so v = -20 m/s. Use v = v0 - gt: -20 = 10 - 10t, giving t = 3 s. For vertical displacement from launch point to ground, -H = v0 t - (1/2)gt^2 = 10(3) - (1/2)(10)(3^2) = 30 - 45 = -15, so H = 15 m. For the cart, set the vertical landing point as x = 0. Initially M is at x = -s = -4 m and N is at x = -(s+L) = -(4+5) = -9 m. The cart starts from rest and moves right with displacement d = (1/2)at^2. For the cart to catch the ball when the ball lands at x = 0, the landing point must lie between the shifted N and M: x_N(t) <= 0 <= x_M(t). This is equivalent to s <= d <= s+L. With t = 3 s, d = (1/2)a(3^2) = (9/2)a, so 4 <= (9/2)a <= 9. Hence 8/9 <= a <= 2 m/s^2.
